Definition: from G1909 and G5495; to put the hand upon, i.e. undertake:--go about, take in hand (upon).
BiblicalUsage: Epicheireo means to take in hand, to undertake — to put the hand to a work. Many have taken in hand to set forth the gospel in order; Paul disputes with the Grecians, who go about to slay him; and the vagabond Jews take upon them to call over the name of the Lord Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: Luke's careful history, Paul's bold dispute, and the exorcists' empty imitation all took something in hand, but the authority was not the same. I believe the word separates the three undertakings: the hand is the same, and only the Name makes the difference.
